title: 2s and 2p orbital energies of hydrogen and lithium - degeneracy, penetration and shielding
summary: A hydrogen atom and a lithium atom in an atom chamber beside an energy ladder. Press start and the bench does the rest: for H 2s, H 2p, Li 2s and Li 2p it solves the radial Schroedinger equation by shooting, draws where the electron is found - orange dots when it is inside the lithium 1s core - puts each energy on the ladder, then tests options (A)-(D) one by one and reveals the true ones. No prediction stage - input, run, watch, result.
subject: Chemistry
topic: Orbital energies - degeneracy in hydrogen, penetration and shielding in lithium
subtopics: Orbital energy of a one-electron atom: E = -13.6 Z^2/n^2 eV, depends on n only
Multi-electron atoms: energy depends on n and l
Shielding by core electrons and effective nuclear charge
Penetration of s versus p orbitals; radial probability distributions
Radial Schroedinger equation and node counting
concepts: In hydrogen there is one electron and nothing to shield it, so the orbital energy depends only on n: E2s(H) = E2p(H) = -13.6/4 = -3.40 eV (degenerate)
In lithium the 2s or 2p electron moves in the field of the +3 nucleus and the 1s2 core; outside the core it feels about +1, inside up to +3
The 2s orbital has a small inner lobe that penetrates the 1s core; the 2p orbital has an angular node at the nucleus and stays mostly outside - so 2s feels a higher effective nuclear charge
Higher effective nuclear charge means lower energy: E2s(Li) < E2p(Li)
Zeff(Li, 2s) is greater than 1 (about 1.26 from the measured energy, 1.30 by Slater's rules), so E2s(Li) is below E2s(H): E2s(H) > E2s(Li)
Since E2p(H) = E2s(H) > E2s(Li), the statement E2p(H) < E2s(Li) is false
formulas: -1/2 u'' + [V(r) + l(l+1)/(2 r^2)] u = E u  (atomic units)
V(r) = -Z/r + field of the 1s core;  zeta(1s) = Z - 5/16

methods: Solved independently before any key was consulted: one-electron degeneracy in H; penetration and shielding in Li
sympy: the hydrogenic 2s and 2p functions are exact eigenfunctions with E = -1/8 hartree = -3.40 eV
Numerical radial Schroedinger equation (Numerov shooting, written separately from the page): H 2s = 2p = -3.401 eV; Li 2s -4.763 eV, Li 2p -3.426 eV in the field of the nucleus and a 1s2 core
Slater's rules: Zeff(Li, 2s) = 1.30, E ~ -5.75 eV < -3.40 eV
Spectroscopy: H n = 2 at -3.40 eV; Li ionisation energy 5.392 eV; Li 670.8 nm resonance line (1.848 eV) gives Li 2p -3.544 eV
Hartree-Fock delta-SCF (pyscf, aug-cc-pVTZ): Li 2s -5.342 eV, Li 2p -3.500 eV
Every data set gives (A), (B), (D) true and (C) false; robust to the core exponent 2.3-3.0; removing the core restores the degeneracy and makes (A) false; Be+ gives the same three
Independent script tests/verify_p1q05.py: 18 of 18 checks pass
Solution websites: MathonGo's published solution (their Q37) gives (A), (B), (D) with the same reasoning
The page solves the four orbitals itself and evaluates each printed statement on its own energies at run time

Headless-browser suite tests/sim_p1q05.js drives the whole page: optional inputs with empty, invalid, negative, fractional, inconsistent and zero entries, the automatic run from one START to the reveal, the solver, the cloud and its inside-the-core count, every option test, every calculation line in order, the reveal and its blink, replay, pause, reset, a no-core custom run ((B), (D)), classroom mode, 390 and 360 px, reduced motion, the feed entries, and the real app shell opening it
Answer cross-checked afterwards against the official final key printed with the Paper 1 PDF: Q5 -> (A), (B), (D)
verification.note: Built to the streamlined specification. The page's core model (nucleus + frozen 1s2 Hartree field, no exchange) under-binds Li 2s (-4.76 against -5.39 eV measured) but gives every inequality in the options the same way; the measured and Hartree-Fock values are shown beside it.

A shooting solver shown live: the wavefunction for each trial energy, its tail flying up or diving down, the energy halving in on the allowed value
Electron clouds of 1400 dots: orange dots mark the electron found inside the 1s core - many for Li 2s, few for Li 2p
An energy ladder that fills level by level, then tests each printed statement by ringing the two levels it compares and marking TRUE or FALSE
A side-by-side view of Li 2s and Li 2p with their inside-the-core counts

A radial probability graph of the four orbitals over the shaded 1s core, and an effective nuclear charge bar chart
A calculation panel with each energy, Zeff, the time spent inside the core and the extra pull from penetration, the degeneracy, the literature check, each option and the answer
The reveal dims the laboratory, flashes, sprays OPTIONS (A), (B), (D) with CONGRATULATIONS, ANSWER FOUND and the energy order, and blinks the header answer once
